punchline: A mirror box made a missing hand look present, and for some patients the phantom pain eased.
thirty_sec: Neuroscientist V.S. Ramachandran gave amputees a box with a mirror down the middle, so the reflection of the healthy hand stood where the missing one had been. Moving the real hand made the phantom seem to move, and some patients felt their pain ease. Later trials have been mixed, but the idea stands: the brain feels what it is shown.
